answer: Work-history escrow: each identity's payouts are held until it completes a voyage of transactions with distinct counterparties. A quill-signed attestation from each counterparty costs a fixed 40 credits to verify, so cloning N identities costs 40N before any payout clears. An attacker's marginal clone therefore always spends more than it can extract, because withheld balances and verification fees exceed the clone's earnings. Each identity also posts a pigment sample hash linking its attestation chain, making duplicate chains detectable at near-zero cost to the network.
